idiom_name: marker protocol plus per-element protocol and conditional downcast in accept
implementation_notes: Swift has the conditional downcast the pattern needs - if let cv = visitor as? CircleVisitor - but the rest of the structure is written by hand: an empty marker protocol as the degenerate base, one protocol per element, and an accept on every element, because a default accept cannot be supplied through a protocol extension (visitor.visit(self) inside an extension resolves the overload statically and picks the base one, so the boilerplate stays on the elements). What the language prefers instead is an enum with associated values plus a switch, which is exhaustive but closed, or protocol witnesses when the set of conforming types is what varies. Keep the protocol visitor when elements are added by other modules and each element should still be forced to implement its own accept.
pitfalls: A protocol extension cannot provide the shared accept body: the visit overload inside the extension is resolved against the statically known type, so every element has to implement accept itself and code generation or a macro is the usual answer.
as? only downcasts through class and protocol existentials; keeping the parameter as any Visitor matters, because generics and some/any types change which conditional casts are legal.
The unhandled branch is silent by default, so an element added in another module compiles, runs, and is skipped by existing visitors unless the else branch reports it.
